study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Ge et al., Lancet Digital Health, 2024
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Normative modelling of brain morphometry across the lifespan with CentileBrain: algorithm benchmarking and model optimisation

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study performed a comparative evaluation of eight algorithms: ordinary least squares regression (OLSR), Bayesian linear regression (BLR), generalised additive models for location, scale, and shape (GAMLSS), parametric Lambda (λ), Mu (μ), Sigma (σ) method (LMS; a subclass of GAMLSS), Gaussian process regression (GPR), warped Bayesian linear regression (WBLR), hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR), and multivariate fractional polynomial regression (MFPR). MFPR emerged as the preferred algorithm due to its accuracy and computational efficiency.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: The data for each morphometric measure were analysed with the following algorithms: (1) ordinary least squares regression (OLSR)... (2) Bayesian linear regression (BLR)... (3) generalised additive models for location, scale, and shape (GAMLSS)... (4) parametric Lambda (λ), Mu (μ), Sigma (σ) method (LMS)... (5) Gaussian process regression (GPR)... (6) warped Bayesian linear regression (WBLR)... (7) hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR)... (8) multivariate fractional polynomial regression (MFPR)... The MFPR emerged as the preferred algorithm

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Normative models were developed for 150 regional morphometry measures: 68 regional cortical thickness measures, 68 regional cortical surface area measures, and 14 subcortical volumetric measures. Global measures including total intracranial volume (TIV), mean cortical thickness, and total surface area were also modeled.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: yield global measures of total intracranial volume, mean cortical thickness, and total surface area, as well as measures of cortical thickness and cortical surface area from the 68 Desikan-Killiany atlas regions and 14 subcortical volumetric measures based on the Aseg atlas. Sex-specific normative models were developed separately for each of the 150 regional morphometry measures

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Explanatory variables included age (with non-linear fractional polynomials), global neuroimaging measures (ICV, mean CT, total surface area), scanner vendor, FreeSurfer version, and Euler's number. Site was also considered as a random effect in some algorithm comparisons.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: Model optimisation involved the evaluation of improvements in the MAE... by adding the following explanatory variables: global neuroimaging measures (ie, intracranial volume, mean cortical thickness, or mean cortical surface area, as appropriate), and both linear and non-linear contributions from these variables were considered; scanner vendor type; FreeSurfer version; Euler's number for scan quality... Optimized models included age and global neuroimaging measures... The top-performing algorithm when the site was used as a random effect was still the MFPR
